messages:
maria: heads-up — i hit a nasty race in host<->gpu handoff when compaction overlaps an eviction. reproducer attached, can show segfaults + a leaked slab.

sam: ouch. any quick repro steps? can you paste the minimal log?

maria: steps are short: heavy allocation churn + forced compaction on the host side while evictor migrates pages back to gpu. minimal log: 
```
E 03:12:07 evictor: started handoff id=42 tenant=42
I 03:12:07 compactor: queued slab=0x7f8 remove-range
E 03:12:07 handoff: race: slab->owner=null check failed
SIGSEGV at 0x0
```

jon: looks like the handoff clears ownership before compactor finishes its walk. we probably need a stronger handshake.

alex: agree. current API is just a boolean 'in_handoff' flag + best-effort refcount. that's fragile under CPU parallel compaction.

rachel: what about an epoched token approach? handoff creates a token we pass to compactor; compactor must return/retire token before we null owner. effectively a two-phase commit for ownership transition.

sam: that would add latency to compaction, though. compaction needs to make progress without stalling every handoff. can we make tokens lightweight and designed for optimistic fast-path?

maria: proposal sketch: 
- handoff creates Token{handoff_id, deadline, sig} and publishes to tenant-handoff-table 
- compactor checks token presence before touching pages; if token exists it retires when done. 
- evictor waits for token retirement or timeout then forces fallback (rebind to host backing)

jon: fallback on timeout is key — we should never block the evictor indefinitely. but if evictor gives up we need a safe fallback to avoid double-free. maybe move to read-copy-update style: compactor operates on snapshots and writes new owner only after snapshot done.

alex: RCU will be heavy to implement across host/gpu boundaries. tokens + timeout seems simpler and explicit. what about telemetry: we need metrics for token wait time, forced timeouts, and handoff failures.

rachel: +1 for metrics. add gauges: handoff_inflight_count, avg_handoff_wait_s, forced_timeouts_count. that'll help tune timeout windows per tenant.

sam: question: where should token lifecycle live? in runtime core or allocator? if allocator owns page metadata it should own tokens. but runtime already orchestrates compaction. 

maria: prefer allocator-owned tokens with runtime helpers to create/observe them. allocator can expose: 
```
create_handoff(tenant_id) -> handoff_id
observe_handoff(handoff_id) -> {state, age_s}
retire_handoff(handoff_id)
```

jon: sounds good. also add an API for 'force_retire' so evictor can escalate and mark pages as demoted-to-host with a safe migration hint. that ensures consistent state transitions.

alex: implementation nit: token checks need to be cheap for hot paths. use atomic pointer in page header to token struct; compactor reads atomic, if non-null bumps local ref and proceeds. retire sets pointer to retired marker and waits for readers to drain (like epoch).

maria: exact implementation detail can be in RFC. for now, action items: 
- i'll open RFC outlining token lifecycle + fallback semantics (maria)
- sam/ jon: can you sketch the allocator API surfaces + minimal perf probes (bench harness)
- alex: add telemetry + traces for handoff flows in observability backlog
- rachel: please review SLA implications for tenant timeouts and suggested defaults

deploy-bot: note: created ticket #RT-1302 and linked to thread.

sam: thanks — i'm a bit worried about memory pressure scenarios where forced timeouts kick in often. RFC should include conservative defaults and a tuning guide.

maria: agreed. i'll include a section on degraded-mode behavior: if forced_timeouts_count > 1% over 1m, recommend lowering compaction aggressiveness and increasing handoff timeout for that tenant.

jon: can we add a short integration test in chaos-suite that runs compactor+evictor under artificial delays and asserts no double-free / no segfaults? that'll be enough to validate correctness + guard rails.

maria: yes — i'll add chaos test blueprint in RFC. ok i'm going to draft RFC now. ping me if you want to pair on the API section. :thumbsup:
